title: GPU availability snapshot and triage - 2026-03-20
summary: Weekly snapshot focused on unexpected NA-west availability dip, short-term triage steps taken, and follow-ups for autoscaling/prewarm policy changes.
body:
Purpose:
Quick status and triage notes for GPU availability across regions. Capture decisions from today's ad-hoc triage meeting and owners for follow-ups. Meant for infra team async catch-up and for handoff to on-call rotation.

Attendees:
- Samir Patel (infra lead)
- Aisha Khan (capacity planning)
- Marcus Li (SRE)
- Ruth Nguyen (serving-runtime liaison)
- Diego Morales (cloud ops)
- Optional: Eva (support) joined for customer impact context

Agenda:
1) NA-west availability blip summary
2) Region-by-region capacity snapshot (SLA vs effective capacity)
3) Short-term mitigations deployed and immediate action items
4) Longer-term follow-ups (prewarm, autoscale tuning, procurement)
5) Open questions / risk points

1) NA-west availability blip (summary)
- Timeline: 2026-03-20 03:10–04:05 UTC we observed a 15–22% drop in available GPU slots for hosted workloads in us-west-2 pool. Tail latency for small-chat fell 40–90ms for high QPS customers during this window.
- Root cause (initial): two rack-level maintenance jobs initiated by cloud provider overlapped with our scheduled rolling kernel update; combined, node drain pressure exceeded our rebalancer buffer. A subsequent scheduled capacity shrink (reserved->on-demand rotation) amplified the visible shortage.
- Impact: No customer-facing 5xxs reported. Several high-traffic customers saw increased 95th percentile latency and elevated token costs. No Dedicated customers affected (isolated pools).

2) Region snapshot (effective capacity / notes) - current at 2026-03-20 09:00 UTC
- NA-west (us-west-2): advertised GPUs: 240, effective available: 188 (78%), avg utilization 72% across seq len 128 workloads. Spare pool after reserved commitments: 12 nodes (~24 cards). Notes: elevated fragmentation (many small-card reservations), some nodes in draining state.
- NA-east (us-east-1): advertised GPUs: 360, effective available: 342 (95%), avg utilization 58%. Healthy.
- EU-central (eu-central-1): advertised GPUs: 210, effective available: 190 (90%), avg utilization 66%. Noted slight disk pressure on 3 nodes; disk cleanup job scheduled.
- APAC-sg (ap-southeast-1): advertised GPUs: 120, effective available: 118 (98%), avg utilization 49%. Good headroom.
- Spot/ephemeral reclaim rate (fleet-wide last 24h): 7.1% (up from 3.6% baseline).

3) Short-term mitigations taken during the incident
- Deployed temporary rebalancer (scripts/tools/rebalancer PR-68) to consolidate small reservations and defragment NA-west pool (Marcus + Diego). Result: recovered ~22 GPUs back into the spare pool by 03:50 UTC.
- Raised autoscale minimum in us-west-2 by +6 nodes to avoid immediate undershoot (Aisha). Will revert after stabilization check tomorrow morning.
- Disabled one non-critical maintenance job window for the region for next 48 hours (Samir).
- Manual KV cache warm transfers for two high-QPS customers to alternative regions to reduce tail risk (Ruth).

4) Immediate action items (owners + ETA)
- INF-1: Run full node health sweep for us-west-2 to ensure no latent drain artifacts (owner: Marcus Li) — ETA: 2026-03-21 12:00 UTC.
- INF-2: Validate rebalancer script idempotency and add circuit breaker on job runtime > 10min (owner: Diego Morales) — ETA: 2026-03-23.
- INF-3: Add a short-term routing policy to prefer eu-central/apac for non-latency-sensitive background evals (owner: Ruth Nguyen) — ETA: 2026-03-22.
- INF-4: Cost note — estimate incremental hourly spend due to raised min-autoscale in us-west-2. Aisha to produce delta (owner: Aisha Khan) — ETA: 2026-03-21 COB.
- INF-5: Support outreach: draft customer note for impacted customers summarizing cause/remediation and steps to mitigate (owner: Eva / support) — ETA: 2026-03-21 10:00 UTC.

5) Longer-term follow-ups (not blockers but prioritized)
- Prewarming policy: run a 2-week experiment to prewarm hot-prefix caches in NA-west for top-20 customers (proposal attached in CONFLUENCE link). Objective: reduce 95th pct tail during maintenance windows. Owner: Samir. Kickoff: 2026-03-24.
- Autoscale tuning: evaluate separate autoscale curves for pooling vs bursty routes (proposal: allow slightly higher min for bursty routes). Owner: Aisha. Analysis by 2026-03-28.
- Procurement ask: consider short-term burst reservation purchase for Q2 to lower spot reclaim exposure in NA-west (ask to finance + sales). Owner: Samir + Marcus. Decision by 2026-03-27.
- Rebalancer hardening: add a dry-run report and historical impact dashboard to monitor fragmentation over time. Owner: Diego. ETA: 2026-04-05.

Open questions / risks
- If the provider schedules overlapping maintenance again, do we want to introduce a global maintenance freeze window for reserved->on-demand rotations? (ops policy question). Owner: Samir to propose.
- Spot reclaim volatility trend: 7.1% yesterday — is this noise or start of a trend? Need 7-day moving average analysis. (Aisha).
- Effect on Dedicated customers if fragmentation grows: currently isolated, but we should simulate worst-case failover. (Marcus).

Notes / misc
- Observability: added a temporary dashboard panel to show 'fragmentation metric' = count of reservations < 4 cards across region. Link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/infra/fragmentation
- Log snippets and timeline attached to JIRA-INFRA-4123. Please append any findings to that ticket.
- We discussed a lightweight 'pause' flag for non-critical infra jobs during provider maintenance windows — seems simple and low-risk; follow-up task to make a small orchestrator change (PR discussion in github PR-71).

Retro / what went well
- Quick cross-team collaboration — SRE + cloud ops + runtime engineered a near-immediate mitigation and prevented wider degradation.
- Rebalancer changes recovered capacity faster than expected.

What to improve
- We need clearer pre-notification ingestion from cloud provider about rack-level maintenance; existing telemetry flagged nodes but not the scheduled maintenance stamp. Action: Marcus to file a provider support escalation.
- Add a weekly region imbalance digest for infra standup so team can spot rising fragmentation trends earlier (Aisha).

Appendix: relevant links and tickets
- JIRA-INFRA-4123 (incident timeline + logs)
- Confluence: https://redwood-confluence/internal/infra/gpu-capacity-playbook
- Rebalancer PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/68
- Grafana panel (fragmentation): https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/infra/fragmentation

If anything missing or if you want me to run a deeper query on per-customer token-cost delta during the window, ping me in #infra-ops and I'll attach the export.

-- Samir
